features.title: Game window and basic rendering
features.user_visible_behavior: A pygame window opens showing a black court, a dashed centre line, two white paddles on the left and right edges, and a white ball in the centre.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Verify a pygame window opens.
Verify the court is black with a dashed centre line.
Verify two white paddles are visible on the left and right edges.
Verify a white ball is visible in the centre.
features.notes: Use pygame. Screen size 900x600. Run at 60 FPS.

features.title: Right paddle — player controlled via arrow keys
features.user_visible_behavior: Pressing UP moves the right paddle up. Pressing DOWN moves the right paddle down. The paddle cannot move beyond the top or bottom of the screen.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Press UP arrow — verify right paddle moves up.
Press DOWN arrow — verify right paddle moves down.
Hold UP until paddle reaches the top — verify it stops at the screen edge.
Hold DOWN until paddle reaches the bottom — verify it stops at the screen edge.
features.notes: Use pygame.K_UP and pygame.K_DOWN. Paddle speed 6px per frame.

features.title: Left paddle — AI controlled using UP/DOWN logic
features.user_visible_behavior: The left paddle automatically tracks the vertical position of the ball using the same UP/DOWN movement logic as the player paddle. It cannot move beyond screen edges.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Observe the left paddle over 30 seconds.
Verify it moves up when the ball is above its centre.
Verify it moves down when the ball is below its centre.
Verify it does not move beyond the top or bottom screen edges.
features.notes: AI must use the same move_up/move_down methods as the player paddle — not a teleport or direct y assignment. This keeps behaviour consistent and testable.

features.title: Ball movement and wall bouncing
features.user_visible_behavior: The ball moves continuously at a constant speed. It bounces off the top and bottom walls by reversing its vertical velocity. It does not bounce off the left or right walls.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Verify the ball moves diagonally from the start.
Verify the ball bounces off the top wall.
Verify the ball bounces off the bottom wall.
Verify the ball does not bounce off the left or right edges.
features.notes: Initial velocity should be randomised in direction. Speed: 5px per frame. Use random.choice([-1, 1]) for x and y direction.

features.title: Ball and paddle collision detection
features.user_visible_behavior: When the ball hits either paddle, it reverses horizontal direction. The bounce angle varies based on where on the paddle the ball makes contact — centre hits go straight, edge hits go at sharper angles.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Let the ball hit the right (player) paddle — verify it bounces back.
Let the ball hit the left (AI) paddle — verify it bounces back.
Hit the ball near the top edge of a paddle — verify a steeper angle.
Hit the ball near the centre of a paddle — verify a flatter angle.
features.notes: Use pygame.Rect.colliderect(). Only bounce if the ball is moving toward the paddle to prevent double-bouncing.

features.title: Score tracking and display
features.user_visible_behavior: When the ball passes the left edge, the right player (human) scores a point. When the ball passes the right edge, the left player (AI) scores a point. Scores are displayed at the top centre of the screen. The ball resets to the centre after each point.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Let the ball pass the left edge — verify right player score increments by 1.
Let the ball pass the right edge — verify left player score increments by 1.
Verify the ball resets to the centre after each score.
Verify scores are displayed on screen throughout.

features.title: Win condition and game over screen
features.user_visible_behavior: The first player to reach 10 points wins. The game pauses and displays a winner message. The player can press R to restart or Escape to quit.
verification: Manually set winning score to 2 for testing.
Let one player reach 2 points.
Verify the game pauses and displays a winner message.
Press R — verify scores reset and the game restarts.
Press Escape — verify the game quits.
features.notes: Winning score is 10 in production. Lower to 2 only for testing, then restore.

features.title: Pause and reset controls
features.user_visible_behavior: Pressing P during a game pauses and unpauses it. Pressing R resets scores and restarts the ball. Pressing Escape quits the game.
verification: Run pong_game.py.
Press P — verify the game pauses (ball and paddles freeze).
Press P again — verify the game resumes.
Press R — verify scores reset to 0 and ball resets to centre.
Press Escape — verify the game window closes.
